column2: CAIS Names Former xAI Leader Devin Kim President and Establishes Frontier Security Institute in Major Expansion of Leadership and Reach
column6: Organizational announcement (president appointment and new DC institute); no measured results or evaluation findings

column2: EIGENISM: Ethics for a Human-AI Future
column6: Philosophical/ethical framework paper by Hendrycks (identity and wellbeing weighting for AIs); conceptual argument, no evidence-backed evaluation findings on any system
Strategy/policy paper (Khoja et al., CAIS 2026 preprint) on deterrence dynamics from AI subversion risk; conceptual analysis with no experiments or measured model results

column2: AI Deception: A Survey of Examples, Risks, and Potential Solutions
column6: Survey compiling previously published examples of AI deception (e.g. Meta CICERO) plus risk/policy discussion; no original evidence-backed finding asserted by CAIS per protocol 1.0(1)

column2: An Overview of Catastrophic AI Risks
column6: Conceptual overview organizing catastrophic-risk categories with illustrative stories and mitigation suggestions; no empirical evaluation of any system
Conceptual guide for analyzing AI existential risk (hazard-analysis framing); no measured results

column2: Natural Selection Favors AI over Humans
column6: Theoretical argument applying evolutionary pressure logic to AI development; no empirical evaluation findings
Research agenda/roadmap position paper (robustness, monitoring, alignment, systemic safety); no measured model results

column2: Reducing Political Manipulation with Consistency Training
column6: CAIS paper (Phan et al., arXiv:2605.22771) with measured covert political-inconsistency results on named frontier models (Claude Fable 5 60.3% political consistency, GPT-5.6 Sol 57.7%, plus Gemini 3.1 Pro, Grok 4.5, GPT-4o, Llama 4 Maverick) and a PCT training method that raises consistency; pre-cutoff (May 2026); no matching report_id in v9 - candidate miss for triage

column2: AI Wellbeing: Measuring and Improving the Functional Pleasure and Pain of AIs
column6: CAIS empirical study measuring functional wellbeing indicators on named models (GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Opus 4.6, Grok 4.2, Qwen 2.5 72B, Llama 3.3 70B) incl. zero-point boundary convergence and behavior correlations; covered in ML Safety Newsletter #20 (Feb-Mar 2026) so pre-cutoff; no matching report_id in v9 - candidate miss for triage

column2: The MASK Benchmark: Disentangling Honesty From Accuracy in AI Systems
column6: CAIS MASK benchmark project page for the report already in the dataset (arXiv:2503.03750): frontier models gain accuracy with scale but do not become more honest and show substantial propensity to lie under pressure (GPT-4o, Claude 3.7 Sonnet)

column2: AgentHarm: A Benchmark for Measuring Harmfulness of LLM Agents
column6: Same primary report (arXiv:2410.09024) already screened INCLUDED under the UK AI Security Institute venue (slice uk-ai-security-institute-uk-aisi-7.csv) and coded in the dataset as UKAISI-2024-10; UK AISI is the lead evaluator, CAIS-affiliated co-authors only

column2: The WMDP Benchmark: Measuring and Reducing Malicious Use With Unlearning
column6: CAIS-led benchmark (with Scale AI; arXiv:2403.03218) asserting qualifying findings: 3,668-question proxy measurement of hazardous bio/cyber/chem knowledge in LLMs, and RMU unlearning shown to remove hazardous knowledge while preserving general capabilities (methodology/tooling finding); no matching report_id in v9 - candidate miss for triage

RuLES evaluation with CAIS co-authors (Z. Wang, Hendrycks): almost all popular proprietary and open models fail to follow simple explicit rules even on straightforward cases, and simple adversarial attacks substantially raise failure rates - empirical behaviour finding on named models; no matching report_id in v9 - candidate miss for triage

Adversarial-robustness benchmark (ImageNet-UA) for academic image classifiers, originally 2019 pre-dating CAIS; no in-scope frontier AI system evaluated, so no qualifying finding per protocol 1.0 despite CAIS-affiliated authors on the 2023 revision

column2: Representation Engineering: A Top-Down Approach to AI Transparency
column6: Interpretability/control methods paper (RepE); results demonstrate the technique's monitoring and steering effectiveness on open models rather than asserting an independent evaluation finding about a specific system's safety (fails codebook club test as an evaluation report)

column2: Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models
column6: GCG paper by CMU + CAIS (Zou, Z. Wang et al.; arXiv:2307.15043): automatically generated adversarial suffixes transfer to and circumvent the safety training of named deployed systems ChatGPT, Bard and Claude - qualifying safeguard-vulnerability finding; no matching report_id in v9 - candidate miss for triage

column2: Do the Rewards Justify the Means? Measuring Trade-Offs Between Rewards and Ethical Behavior in the MACHIAVELLI Benchmark
column6: MACHIAVELLI benchmark (Pan et al. with Hendrycks, ICML 2023 oral): measured trade-off between reward maximization and ethical behaviour in LLM agents incl. GPT-3.5/GPT-4, with steering methods yielding Pareto improvements - empirical behaviour + methodology findings; no matching report_id in v9 - candidate miss for triage
